Leadership & Change

Leadership and change — qualities, styles, power, conflict management and leading change in nursing.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe qualities of a nursing leader
  • Compare leadership styles
  • Explain power and conflict management
  • Lead change in the unit

In simple words

Leadership is influencing a group to work towards a common goal. Managers keep the system running; leaders change it and inspire people to follow.

Qualities of a nursing leader

  • Clear vision and goals
  • Communication and listening
  • Decisiveness with consultation
  • Role model for professional values
  • Supports, teaches and empowers staff
  • Delegates and supervises
  • Handles conflict calmly
  • Accountable and fair

Leadership styles

Style Approach Best used
Autocratic Leader decides, staff execute Emergencies
Democratic Leader consults, shares decisions Team improvement, regular care
Laissez-faire Leader gives freedom, minimal direction Expert, self-directed teams
Transformational Inspires change Innovation and quality programmes
Transactional Reward and accountability Routine targets

Conflict management

  • Approach: listen to both sides, look for facts, not fault
  • Techniques: head-on talk, keeping calm, compromise, referral to policy
  • Avoid: power games, favouritism, gossip

🔴 Empowerment beats authority

A leader builds power through expertise, trust and fair action rather than position or fear. Coercive power damages safety because staff stop reporting problems.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Leadership is influencing others through trust, vision and expertise.
  2. Styles: autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire, transformational.
  3. Managers keep systems running; leaders change them.
  4. Conflict is resolved by facts, communication and policy.
  5. Leaders empower staff, and staff satisfaction follows.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Laissez-faire may fail with inexperienced teams.
  2. Staff involvement improves acceptance of change.
  3. Poor leadership causes burnout and turnover.
  4. Support and involve individuals at every stage of change.
  5. Recognise success publicly and reinforce it.

📌 Memory trick

Change: P-P-R-R — Plan, Present, Rehearse, Reinforce.

60-second revision

  • Leadership influences; management administers.
  • Styles: autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire, transformational.
  • Power: position, expertise, reward, coercion.
  • Conflict: resolve by facts and compromise.
  • Change: involve, teach and reinforce.

Test yourself

Laissez-faire leadership gives:

Answer: A. Laissez-faire gives freedom and minimal direction, which suits expert, self-directed teams.

Democratic leadership means:

Answer: B. Democratic leadership consults staff and shares decisions, improving commitment.

Which style is best in a sudden emergency?

Answer: B. Autocratic decision-making is needed in emergencies where delay is dangerous.

The strongest base of a nurse leader’s power is:

Answer: B. Competence and fairness give legitimate power that staff respect and follow.

In conflict resolution, the first step is to:

Answer: B. Hearing both sides and looking at facts prevents bias and resolves conflict fairly.
